subject: MAP: Performance orchestration and variant runbook for CardioTech close
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Alex Li <alex.li@cardiotech.com>, Carmen Soto <carmen.soto@cardiotech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: Performance orchestration and variant runbook for CardioTech close

Alex / Carmen —

Thanks for the sync today. As promised, I’m attaching the MAP-oriented performance plan that we'll use to qualify a final model variant and sign the SOW. High-level goals we agreed on:

- Production SLO targets (CardioTech app):
  - Time to First Token (TTFT) target: <= 220 ms
  - p50 latency (response generation): <= 200 ms
  - p95 latency: <= 450 ms
  - Sustained throughput: >= 2,000 tokens/sec for batching profile B
  - Concurrency target: support 120 simultaneous interactive sessions under 300ms p50 guardrail
  - Quality: intent classification accuracy >= 92% on CardioTech eval set; hallucination rate < 3%

- Execution windows:
  - Week 1: baseline profiling (hosted endpoints, no shadowing)
  - Week 2: controlled variant A/B evaluation (quality + perf)
  - Week 3: production shadowing + final sign-off

Attached: MAP-Perf-Test-Plan.csv (test cases, telemetry hooks, and acceptance criteria) and variant-eval-scripts.sh (load test harness and evaluation runner).

Please confirm the following so we can lock dates:
1) Final approval to run shadow traffic in Week 3 (we’ll cap at 10% traffic and provide replay controls)
2) Any additional compliance checks we should include in the runbook (data retention TTLs, masking flags)
3) Whether a dedicated IP allowlist is required for the test endpoints

Next steps (internal): Marissa, Ben — I’ll need the lab baseline numbers for the three shortlisted variants (see CSV). Can you also add the telemetry GUIDs for intent/QA metrics to the plan?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: MAP-Perf-Test-Plan.csv (CSV), variant-eval-scripts.sh (shell script)

Aditya —

Thanks for the clear plan. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we greenlight:

- For concurrency, the "120 sessions" figure is our 95th percentile peak. Can you confirm whether your load harness will simulate realistic think-times (we have ~5s mean think-time between user messages)?
- On quality metrics: we’ll provide a 3k-example holdout set that includes edge-case device telemetry phrases — please advise if tokenization differences across variants will affect scoring (we prefer your team to canonicalize).
- For Week 3 shadowing: procurement will need an IP allowlist and a short data-processing addendum (DPA addendum) in place. Carmen, can you coordinate with Redwood procurement?

Assuming those are fine, we’re ready to proceed on Monday.

— Alex
Director of Product, CardioTech
alex.li@cardiotech.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 6 Jul 2027 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Performance orchestration and variant runbook for CardioTech close

Aditya / Ben / Alex —

Quick note on test harness and expected lab baselines (we ran an internal dry-run yesterday against the same workload profile). Summary below — these are single-region Redwood-hosted endpoints with TX batching profile B (batch size distribution 1/2/4/8).

Variant candidates (short names):
- rw-v1-m-70b-quant (70B quantized, aggressive kernel paths)
- rw-v1-s-13b-int8 (13B mixed-int8)
- open-m-7b-8bit (open 7B, 8-bit optimized)

Measured lab baselines (median of 10 runs):
- rw-v1-m-70b-quant: TTFT 210 ms, p50 185 ms, p95 420 ms, throughput 2,200 tok/s (sustained), max stable concurrency 110
- rw-v1-s-13b-int8: TTFT 140 ms, p50 120 ms, p95 340 ms, throughput 1,600 tok/s, max stable concurrency 160
- open-m-7b-8bit: TTFT 95 ms, p50 85 ms, p95 270 ms, throughput 1,100 tok/s, max stable concurrency 200

Quality (internal eval on CardioTech smallholdout — 600 examples):
- rw-v1-m-70b-quant: intent accuracy 94.1%, hallucination rate 1.4%
- rw-v1-s-13b-int8: intent accuracy 92.7%, hallucination rate 2.2%
- open-m-7b-8bit: intent accuracy 88.5%, hallucination rate 4.8%

Observations: rw-v1-m-70b-quant meets quality targets cleanly and meets throughput; latency is slightly higher than 13B for p50 but within TTFT. The 13B is a strong cost/latency tradeoff, and the 7B is attractive for ultra-low latency but misses quality.

Test harness notes (for Aditya / Alex):
- We’ll run two phases each day: 1) synthetic RPS profile to measure kernel throughput and 2) replay of production logs (sanitized) for intent/QA scoring.
- Telemetry hooks will emit per-request GUIDs, p50/p95, token counts, and an intent_accuracy indicator to the shared Drive CSV (see link).

Ben — please add the endpoint names and the test credentials to the MAP spreadsheet and include the allowlist IPs for CardioTech. Alex — for tokenization canonicalization, we’ll preprocess CardioTech examples with Redwood tokenizer v1 before scoring.

-Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Subject: MAP results: lab summary and recommended variant for close

Alex / Carmen —

We completed the Week 2 controlled evaluations and the Week 3 shadowing window (10% traffic, sanitized). Below is a condensed results summary (full CSV: lab-results-20270712.csv attached / Drive link above).

Aggregated production-shadow results (median of shadowed requests):
- rw-v1-m-70b-quant:
  - TTFT: 208 ms | p50: 182 ms | p95: 415 ms
  - Sustained throughput: 2,150 tok/s (batch profile B)
  - Observed stable concurrency: 105 (beyond that we saw queueing latency spikes)
  - Quality: intent accuracy 93.8% | hallucination rate 1.6%
  - Notes: Best quality; unit cost higher but within projected SOW economics with reserved capacity commit.

- rw-v1-s-13b-int8:
  - TTFT: 135 ms | p50: 118 ms | p95: 335 ms
  - Sustained throughput: 1,620 tok/s
  - Observed stable concurrency: 155
  - Quality: intent accuracy 92.4% | hallucination rate 2.1%
  - Notes: Strong latency/cost tradeoff; quality slightly below 70B but within MAP tolerance for standard flows.

- open-m-7b-8bit:
  - TTFT: 98 ms | p50: 90 ms | p95: 260 ms
  - Sustained throughput: 1,120 tok/s
  - Observed stable concurrency: 190
  - Quality: intent accuracy 88.2% | hallucination rate 5.0%
  - Notes: Low latency but does not meet quality targets for safety-sensitive flows.

Recommendation (for CardioTech close):
- Prime variant: rw-v1-m-70b-quant (meets quality and throughput targets; fits SLO envelope).
- Canary plan: start production with rw-v1-s-13b-int8 for non-critical customer segments to reduce unit cost; ramp to rw-v1-m-70b-quant for core flows within 30 days.
- Autoscaling policy: keep headroom for 20% burst concurrency, configure warm pool of 20 GPUs for the 70B variant.

Required procurement items before signing SOW:
- IP allowlist (CardioTech provided)
- Short DPA addendum signed by both parties
- Reserved capacity commit (monthly) signoff for projected usage (Ben, I’ll hand this to you to finalize pricing)

Alex — can you confirm acceptance of the recommendation and whether the procurement items can be completed by EOD Friday (2027-07-16)? If yes, I’ll circulate the final SOW and schedule the DocuSign.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Thanks — the summary is helpful and aligned with our expectations. We accept the recommendation to prime on rw-v1-m-70b-quant with the 13B canary approach. Procurement will circulate the IP allowlist and the DPA addendum by tomorrow. We aim to complete procurement steps by 2027-07-16.
